edits.name: 01-Foot
edits.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1 is the EXACT already-approved game tile to edit, not a loose inspiration. Make a restrained DETAIL PASS on this image, not a redesign. Preserve the original position and shapes of all major rock planes. Preserve all original colors, overall value, near-vertical cliff look, simple pixel-art style and square full-bleed framing.
It is a TRUE 16x16 logical-pixel asset, nearest-neighbor enlarged. Preserve this EXACT coarse 16-by-16 grid. One logical pixel is 1/16 of the width/height. Added details must use whole logical pixels, never tiny subpixels. No antialiasing, blurry gradients, surface noise, dithering or increased resolution.
Add only a few short secondary fracture branches, angular chips and slight breaks in existing rock planes, with detail concentrated along existing crevices. Approximately 15-25 logical pixels may change, while the large shapes remain recognizable and most pixels stay identical. New fine fractures are one logical pixel wide and 2-3 logical pixels long. Keep large quiet patches.
Use ONLY existing exact colors: #A08043 ochre base, #B3995C light tan planes, #805B32 brown shade, #514332 deep crease. Grass colors, when present, are fixed #89A043 and #647B36. Do not brighten the palette. No white or yellow specular highlights.
Preserve the ENTIRE outermost pixel frame: first/last row and first/last column must be exactly as the input. This preserves neighboring tile seams. No grass added to rock, no new objects, pebbles, boulders, vegetation, lettering, border, padding, panels, gridlines or shadows outside the original shapes.
Return only the edited single square tile, no before/after layout.
Specific part: mountain FOOT. Keep the lower quarter (logical rows 12-15) exactly unchanged: same green grass and same contact-shadow silhouette. Add a few subtle jagged stress cracks and small angular chips ONLY within the brown rock of rows 1-11. Do not make separate stones at the base. Keep the wall standing upright against the ground. The entire first row remains solid #A08043.
